title: One‑page customer decisions & verification links for active inference incident
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, customer-facing draft you can copy to Statuspage or email to affected tenants. It focuses on concise decision choices we are offering customers (replay options, evidence links, SLA choices), the plain-language summary of what happened, and verification steps customers can take. Use this as a single-page appendix to the fuller technical postmortem.

Intended audience:
- Primary: impacted tenant engineering and product owners
- Secondary: partner success / account teams who need a single action list to give customers

Current status (short):
- Incident window: 2026-07-19 02:37 UTC — 2026-07-19 06:12 UTC
- Impact: intermittent elevated latency and occasionally truncated structured responses for ~18% of requests in eu-west-1 during the window
- Service state: fully recovered; requests routed to fallback model variants during mitigation window

Plain-language cause summary (for customers):
A routing bug in our autoscale routing layer caused some requests to be forwarded to a model variant that was temporarily misconfigured for KV cache handling. That misconfiguration led to delayed responses and, in a subset of requests, incomplete structured outputs. We detected the mismatch via anomaly alerts and activated the fallback routing policy; we then rolled a config fix and validated normal behavior across tenants.

What we did (customer-facing timeline):
- 02:37 UTC: Alerts triggered — increased p95/p99 latency in eu-west-1
- 02:42 UTC: Auto-fallback route enabled (immediate mitigation; reduced impact but increased token costs for a few tenants)
- 03:15 UTC: Identified config delta in KV cache handler for certain model variant (internal tag: model-v3-quant)
- 04:05 UTC: Config rollback and targeted rollout of corrected variant
- 05:10 UTC: End-to-end verification run (synthetic prompts + tenant-sample validation) — no truncated structured outputs observed
- 06:12 UTC: Normal routing resumed; incident declared resolved after monitoring window

Customer options (choose one). Short snippets you can paste into a customer email or status update:
1) Replay with evidence verification (recommended for customers needing deterministic reconciliation)
   - What we offer: We will re-run affected requests on the corrected model variant and provide an evidence package (original request ids, timestamps, corrected outputs, hashes) for you to validate.
   - Timeline: 48–72 hours depending on volume.
   - Action: Reply to this message with your tenant ID and the time range you want replayed.

2) Opt-in selective replay (cost-limited)
   - What we offer: We will only replay the subset of requests you nominate (e.g., customer-facing API calls or a specific session id list).
   - Timeline: 24–48 hours for small batches (<1000 requests).
   - Action: Provide a CSV with request ids or session ids and the preferred replay priority (high/normal/low).

3) Audit-only evidence package (no replay)
   - What we offer: Full evidence package (request ids, timestamps, original and corrected outputs) so you can perform your own reconciliation offline. No re-execution of requests.
   - Timeline: 24 hours.
   - Action: Reply with tenant ID and preferred secure transfer method (S3 presigned link / secure FTP).

4) SLA credit request (if you experienced measurable customer P90/P99 impact)
   - What we offer: If you can show measurable, customer-facing SLO breaches tied to this incident, we will triage credit eligibility under your contract.
   - Action: Open a support case (INC-4821) quoting the impacted time range and attach performance metrics.

Verification / evidence links (for customers):
- Incident timeline & internal notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-4821-root-cause-notes
- Evidence package sample (redacted): https://storage.redwood.ai/evidence/INC-4821/sample-evidence.zip
- Replay consent form (short): https://forms.redwood.ai/replay-consent?inc=4821

Minimal customer action checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Confirm tenant ID and preferred option (1 / 2 / 3 / 4)
- [ ] If choosing replay, provide request id list or time range
- [ ] If choosing evidence-only, confirm secure transfer method

Technical addendum (short, optional for engineering contacts):
- Root cause: configuration drift in routing metadata that caused an older model variant to be favored for certain sequence-length buckets; that variant had an out-of-sync KV cache compaction setting which led to race conditions for structured outputs.
- Fixes implemented: validated rollback of variant config, added a config-change gating check in deployment pipeline, extended synthetic coverage for sequence-length distribution.
- Preventive work: automated drift detection rule in config-store (deploying in next 2 weeks), additional post-deploy synthetic sweep for model variants, improved runbook for manual rollback.

How we verified recovery:
- Synthetic sweep across sequence length distributions (0.5–12k tokens) with tenant-simulated prompts
- Tenant-sample replays for 3 high-impact customers (redacted) showed parity with pre-incident outputs
- 72-hour monitoring window with no recurrence

Communication templates (short copy ready for statuspage or email):
- Statuspage (short): "Resolved — Between 02:37–06:12 UTC on 2026-07-19 some requests in eu-west-1 experienced higher latency and occasional truncated structured outputs due to a routing configuration issue. The issue is resolved; we are offering replays and evidence packages to affected customers. See action choices and evidence links: <link>."

- Email snippet to tenant with recommended action (concise): "Hi — we detected and resolved a routing misconfiguration that affected some of your requests on 2026-07-19. We can replay affected requests (recommended) or supply an evidence package — please pick an option and we’ll proceed. For full notes and verification artifacts: <link>."

Open questions / dependencies (internal notes to customer-success):
- Need product/serving confirmation on expected increased cost exposure for tenants where fallback route was used; list of impacted tenants required for billing contact.
- Confirm S3 presigned evidence packaging workflow and retention policy with security.
- Legal: any obligations to notify partners beyond SLA (for enterprise accounts) — confirm with AMs.

Owner / escalation path (who to CC):
- Primary CS owner: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Technical lead: Jonas Becker (jonas@redwood.ai)
- Incident commander: Evan Morales (evan@redwood.ai)

Notes to writer:
- Keep the statuspage text <= 280 characters where possible; link to the full evidence package/consent form rather than embedding long lists.
- Use customer-friendly language; avoid internal jargon (e.g., 'KV compaction' should be explained or omitted from customer-facing text).

Revision history:
- 2026-07-19 initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2026-07-20 added replay templates and evidence links (E. Morales)
- 2026-08-02 updated timeline & verification steps after final RCA (J. Becker)

End of doc.
